question.text: Manoj's investment adviser establishes advance ground rules: "If equity allocation exceeds 65% of the portfolio, we will automatically rebalance by booking partial profits." This pre-agreed rule is an example of:

answer.text: Mental Accounting — creating separate buckets for different asset classes
Nudging — a built-in mechanism that ensures disciplined rebalancing by exploiting status quo bias positively
Anchoring — fixating on the 65% figure as an arbitrary reference point
Framing — presenting rebalancing as profit booking to make it palatable

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says that advance ground rules for asset rebalancing create built-in nudges — booking profits when asset prices rise and buying when prices are low. It also explicitly links a simple nudge to status quo bias, so a pre-agreed 65% equity trigger is the workbook's nudging mechanism in action. The Trap: Mental accounting is about bucketing money by source. Anchoring would require fixation on the 65% number rather than using it as an automatic trigger. Framing is about how facts are described, which is a separate phenomenon from the structural pre-commitment described here. Note: When the prompt features a pre-agreed rebalancing rule designed to overcome inertia, identify it as nudging anchored in the workbook's status quo bias discussion.
